claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 791 2.3: "Addresses are fixed length of four octets (32 bits)." RFC 1122 3.3.4 describes a multihomed host as having multiple IP addresses. Live `ip -4 addr` in donhang-lab: "inet 127.0.0.1/8 scope host lo" and "inet 172.28.0.12/24 ... eth0" (one machine, two addresses).
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791.txt 2.3; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122.txt 3.3.4; docker exec donhang-lab (stage-0 image, live run 2026-09-27)

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9293 3.1: "Source Port: 16 bits. The source port number." "Destination Port: 16 bits. The destination port number." A 16-bit unsigned field holds 0..65535.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.txt 3.1

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 1122 3.2.1.3 (g) { 127, <any> }: "Internal host loopback address. Addresses of this form MUST NOT appear outside a host." Lesson says "usually 127.0.0.1", consistent with the whole /8 being loopback. Live: "inet 127.0.0.1/8 scope host lo".
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122.txt 3.2.1.3 (g); docker exec donhang-lab (stage-0 image, live run 2026-09-27)

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 6761 6.3 item 1: "Users may assume that IPv4 and IPv6 address queries for localhost names will always resolve to the respective IP loopback address." With RFC 1122 (g) (loopback never leaves the host), localhost names the machine running the command.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6761.txt 6.3

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 1918 3: "10.0.0.0 - 10.255.255.255 (10/8 prefix) 172.16.0.0 - 172.31.255.255 (172.16/12 prefix) 192.168.0.0 - 192.168.255.255 (192.168/16 prefix)"; "packets with private source or destination addresses should not be forwarded across such links." Compose ipam "subnet: 172.28.0.0/24" lies inside 172.16/12.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918.txt 3; examples/don-hang docker-compose.yml @ stage-0

claim_verdicts.evidence: compose @ stage-0: lab "ipv4_address: 172.28.0.12", db "ipv4_address: 172.28.0.11", ipam "subnet: 172.28.0.0/24", lab ports "8080:8080"; up.sh runs `docker compose up -d --build --wait`. Docker docs: `-p 8080:80` "creates a mapping between port 8080 on any address on the Docker host, and the container's port 80."
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang docker-compose.yml, scripts/up.sh @ stage-0; refs/docker-docs/content/manuals/engine/network/port-publishing.md l.13-15

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live: `timeout 2 nc -l 2222` (root) -> "nc: Address in use", rc=1; same as uid dev. sshd.pam is the 2222 holder (ps). Refusal of a non-sharing later asker on 8080 also confirmed: `busybox nc -l -p 8080` -> "nc: bind: Address in use". Mechanism and SSH example hold; "most [programs] ... do not" is a population count no document or run supports.
claim_verdicts.source: docker exec donhang-lab (stage-0 image, live run 2026-09-27); examples/don-hang docker-compose.yml @ stage-0 (LISTEN_PORT 2222)
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Programs can ask to share a number, but the SSH server does not. That is why your own program, which did not ask to share, could not have 8080: Caddy already had it.
